concepts.title: Somatic Trauma Theory
concepts.excerpt: Here is the simplest version: your body mobilized enormous energy to survive something.

concepts.title: Freeze Response and Immobility
concepts.excerpt: Fight and flight get the press. The organism mobilizes — either toward the threat (attack) or away from it (escape) — and this mobilization is the story we tell about survival.

concepts.title: The Brain Architecture of Trauma
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a smoke detector that cannot be reset. It went off during the fire — correct and necessary.

concepts.title: Felt Sense and Somatic Awareness
concepts.excerpt: Before a thought forms, before a word arrives, before the rational mind has assembled an assessment — the body already knows.

concepts.title: Primal Pain: The Foundational Wound
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a newborn with a basic need—hunger, warmth, touch, safety—going unmet.

concepts.title: Imprinting: How Early Experience Becomes Biology
concepts.excerpt: Imprinting is not memory in the usual sense. You don't remember being imprinted; you are imprinted.

concepts.title: Critical Periods and Imprinting Susceptibility
concepts.excerpt: The nervous system is not equally vulnerable at all ages. There are specific developmental windows—critical periods—when the brain and body are maximally plastic, maximally open to imprinting.

concepts.title: Gating Mechanism: Endorphin-Mediated Repression
concepts.excerpt: The conventional model of repression suggests you "forget" something painful and it sinks into the unconscious.

concepts.title: Emotional vs. Narrative Memory: Distinct Storage Systems
concepts.excerpt: Memory is not one thing. The brain stores experience in fundamentally different ways depending on what and when the experience occurred.

concepts.title: The Three Lines of Consciousness: Brainstem, Limbic, and Cortical Storage
concepts.excerpt: The brain is not one thing. It is layers, each evolved at different times, each capable of independent trauma storage, each requiring its own type of healing.

concepts.title: Compounding: How Early Imprints Are Reinforced by Similar Events
concepts.excerpt: One traumatic event in childhood imprints. A series of similar events compounds that imprint—each reinforcement deepens it, locks it tighter, makes it more rigid and more controlling of personality.

concepts.title: The Reticular Activating System: Chronic Hypervigilance
concepts.excerpt: In a healthy nervous system, the RAS activates when threat is present and deactivates when you're safe.

concepts.title: Somatization: How Psychological Imprints Become Physical Symptoms
concepts.excerpt: Somatization is the term for psychological material expressing as physical symptoms—pain, dysfunction, illness.

concepts.title: The Anxiety Hierarchy: Paths to Psychosis
concepts.excerpt: When gated First Line trauma begins to break through repression, it doesn't emerge as a discrete memory.

concepts.title: Birth Prototype: Personality Determined at Birth
concepts.excerpt: Birth is trauma. The fetus experiences a radical transition: from fluid warmth and constant oxygen to dry air, cold, struggle, pressure, and the effort of the first breath.

concepts.title: The Prototype in Action: Birth Imprint Manifesting as Adult Patterns
concepts.excerpt: The birth prototype is abstract—a determination of sympathetic vs. parasympathetic baseline.

concepts.title: Depression as Parasympathetic State
concepts.excerpt: The conventional model treats depression as a mental illness—a disorder of neurotransmitters, a disease process that requires medication to "fix."

concepts.title: Acting Out: Neurotic Mastery and Behavioral Reenactment
concepts.excerpt: Acting out is not random behavior. It is the organism's sophisticated, though ultimately futile, attempt to resolve an imprinted trauma by recreating it and achieving a different ending.

concepts.title: Neurotic vs. Authentic Self: The Personality Before and After Reliving
concepts.excerpt: Conventional psychology treats personality as relatively fixed and stable—traits, patterns, structures that define who someone is.

concepts.title: Kindling and Trauma Perpetuation
concepts.excerpt: You put out the campfire. You're sure of it — you poured water on the coals, watched the steam rise, felt the heat die down.

concepts.title: Autonomic Oscillation
concepts.excerpt: Your nervous system has two gears: a gas pedal and a brake.

concepts.title: Renegotiation vs. Re-enactment
concepts.excerpt: A cheetah kills a gazelle. The cheetah cubs, watching from a distance, do not immediately attempt to replicate the hunt.

concepts.title: Trauma Reenactment and the Endorphin Mechanism
concepts.excerpt: One of the most mystifying things trauma does is pull people back toward versions of what hurt them.

concepts.title: Somatic Dissociation
concepts.excerpt: A woman who survived sexual assault develops chronic pelvic pain that no gynecologist can explain.

concepts.title: Dissociation and Cognitive Freeze
concepts.excerpt: The body may still be there — sitting in the chair, lying on the ground, continuing to drive the car.

concepts.title: Alexithymia and Speechless Terror
concepts.excerpt: There is a particular kind of session that trauma therapists describe.

concepts.title: Reliving as Healing: Full Autonomic Discharge and Integration
concepts.excerpt: Talk therapy is predicated on a theory of change: understanding trauma, gaining insight, revising narrative.

concepts.title: Integration After Reliving: Post-Healing Reorganization
concepts.excerpt: Reliving resolves the imprint, but the person doesn't return to who they were before trauma.

concepts.title: Diseases of Traumatic Stress
concepts.excerpt: Imagine your body has a fire department. When the alarm sounds, the department mobilizes: adrenaline floods the system, inflammation rises, energy gets diverted from maintenance to emergency.

concepts.title: Sources of Trauma: A Taxonomy
concepts.excerpt: Common sense says trauma is about what happened. The more severe the event, the more traumatic it is.

concepts.title: Trauma Therapy: A Neurobiological Framework
concepts.excerpt: Most trauma therapy — at least in the twentieth century — was organized around the story.

concepts.title: Character as Procedural Learning
concepts.excerpt: Think about how you ride a bike. You don't consult a manual. You don't consciously calculate the angle of lean required for each turn.

concepts.title: Societal and Cultural Trauma
concepts.excerpt: Before the argument about collective trauma can be made, it needs biological grounding.

concepts.title: Delayed Traumatic Reactions
concepts.excerpt: The nervous system, after surviving a traumatic event, does not always generate symptoms immediately.

concepts.title: Character Armor and Muscular Tension
concepts.excerpt: Wilhelm Reich, Lowen's teacher, coined the term "character armor"—the concept that psychological defense becomes literally embodied in the musculature and posture of the body.

concepts.title: Breathing Work and Parasympathetic Activation
concepts.excerpt: The autonomic nervous system (sympathetic and parasympathetic) is called "autonomic" because it functions automatically — the person does not consciously decide to increase heart rate or dilate pupils.

concepts.title: The Grounding Exercise
concepts.excerpt: Many defended individuals exist in a state of being chronically "ungrounded."

concepts.title: Bioenergetic Therapy and Nervous System Reorganization
concepts.excerpt: Talk therapy can provide insight, understanding, and intellectual clarity.

concepts.title: Implicit Memory and Embodied Affect: How Trauma Lives in the Body Beyond Words
concepts.excerpt: Neuroscience has revealed a fundamental truth: trauma is not stored primarily in explicit memory (the conscious narrative "this happened to me").

concepts.title: State-Dependent Memory and Somatic Unconscious: How Trauma Freezes in the Body
concepts.excerpt: Trauma memory is not stored like ordinary memory. It is encoded in the nervous system's state at the moment of threat.

concepts.title: Affect Tolerance and the Gateway to Transformation: The Threshold Between Dissociation and Integration
concepts.excerpt: At the heart of trauma recovery lies a paradox: healing requires feeling the very emotions that trauma made unbearable.

concepts.title: Bilateral Brain Integration in Trauma Recovery: The Conversation Between Two Worlds
concepts.excerpt: Imagine your brain as a divided mansion with two wings. The left wing is the librarian—it catalogues, labels, narrates, makes sense of things in sequence.

concepts.title: Completion and the Finished Survival Response: Nervous System Integration
concepts.excerpt: Kalsched emphasizes a principle that distinguishes his framework from much conventional trauma therapy: the nervous system has an inherent drive toward completion — toward finishing what was interrupted, toward discharging what was frozen, toward completing the survival response that was left unfinished at the moment of trauma.

concepts.title: Embodied Presence and Somatic Unconscious: The Body's Silent Archive
concepts.excerpt: The body is not a vehicle the mind drives. It is not a puppet the brain controls.

concepts.title: Fairbairn's Bad Objects and Early Relational Trauma: When the Person You Depend On Is the Threat
concepts.excerpt: Fairbairn made a radical discovery that overturned classical psychoanalysis: the traumatized person does not repress desires or instincts.

concepts.title: False Self vs. True Self in Trauma: The Hollow Adaptation and the Imprisoned Authenticity
concepts.excerpt: Winnicott distinguished between the true self (authentic, spontaneous, feeling-based, vulnerable) and the false self (adaptive, compliant, protective, disconnected from genuine feeling).

concepts.title: Malignant Regression vs. Adaptive Regression: Fantasy as Dissociative Self-Hypnosis
concepts.excerpt: Regression appears in trauma survivors in two fundamentally different forms that require different clinical responses.

concepts.title: Touching and Holding in Therapeutic Relationship
concepts.excerpt: Few questions present more compelling dilemmas for therapists than the question of physical contact with clients.

concepts.title: Therapeutic Integration of Body and Psyche
concepts.excerpt: Western psychology has traditionally treated the mind and the body as separate domains.

concepts.title: Intergenerational Trauma and Continuity: How Societies Process Catastrophe and Transmit Survival Across Generations
concepts.excerpt: Spanish conquest was traumatic event of catastrophic scale: political structures collapsed, religious worldview was invalidated, population died from epidemic disease, authority figures were subordinated, economic systems were reorganized, cultural practices were prohibited.

concepts.title: Prenatal Consciousness and Sentience
concepts.excerpt: Before you had a word for anything, you were already paying attention.

concepts.title: Prenatal and Perinatal Alienation
concepts.excerpt: Most psychological models locate the original wounding in early childhood — the developmental period when relational experiences shape the attachment templates, the shame system, the ego-structure.

concepts.title: Orpha and the Traumatic Progression: Stages of Overwhelming
concepts.excerpt: Orpha is an archetype appearing in Kalsched's material that represents something often invisible in trauma work: the progression of overwhelming, the way defenses must escalate as threat deepens, and the logic behind why a person's current defense structure is not pathology but necessary evolution.

concepts.title: Holotropic Breathwork and Transpersonal Experience
concepts.excerpt: Most psychotherapy operates at the level of what a person can remember, articulate, and examine.

concepts.title: Transitional Space and Play: The Sacred In-Between Where Healing Becomes Possible
concepts.excerpt: Winnicott identified a paradoxical space in human development: neither fully inner (subjective, fantasy, imagination) nor fully outer (objective, material, consensus reality), but genuinely between.

concepts.title: Transitional Space and Trauma: When the Protective Container Becomes a Trap
concepts.excerpt: In healthy development, the transitional space gradually expands. The child learns to engage with reality while maintaining the capacity for creativity and imagination.

concepts.title: Kundalini and Psychological Transformation: Nervous System Awakening as Crisis and Development
concepts.excerpt: Kundalini, in spiritual traditions, is described as a dormant energy coiled at the base of the spine (root chakra) that can be awakened through practice, initiatory experience, or spontaneous activation.

concepts.title: Chakra System: The Seven Psychological Centers
concepts.excerpt: The chakra system describes human consciousness as a vertical stack of seven operational centers, each governing a distinct bandwidth of psychological function.

concepts.title: Shame as Survival System
concepts.excerpt: Shame is not a moral failing or a character defect. It is an evolved survival mechanism: the nervous system's response to the threat of tribal exclusion.

concepts.title: Tapas as Spiritual Catalyst
concepts.excerpt: Tapas (Sanskrit: तपस्, from root tap — "to heat, to burn") is the most ancient named concept for difficulty as spiritual catalyst in the Indian traditions.

concepts.title: Deprivation Across Generations: The Intergenerational Transmission of Trauma and Defensive Patterns
concepts.excerpt: Cross-Domain Mechanism: Psychology explains how early deprivation creates defensive character structures that shape the person's relationships and parenting.

concepts.title: Epigenetic Inheritance: How Trauma Becomes Biological Legacy
concepts.excerpt: The central dogma of genetics for decades was: DNA sequence determines biology.

concepts.title: Friction and Dissociative Delay: When Plans Meet Interrupted Activation
concepts.excerpt: Clausewitz identified a phenomenon that separates theoretical military strategy from its actual execution: friction.

concepts.title: Protective Equilibrium as Mixed Strategy: The Game Theory of Trauma Defense
concepts.excerpt: Game theory identifies a class of problems where two or more players each have incentives that are not perfectly aligned, and each must choose a strategy knowing that other players are also choosing strategically.

concepts.title: The Contemplative Path to Integration: How Meditation Reorganizes the Nervous System Beyond Psychology
concepts.excerpt: Cross-Domain Mechanism: Psychology explains how early deprivation creates defensive character structures and blocked emotional access.

concepts.title: The Somatic-Psychological Circuit: Why Body and Mind Cannot Be Separated in Healing
concepts.excerpt: Cross-Domain Mechanism: The body and mind are not separate information systems that occasionally communicate.

concepts.title: Trauma and the Nervous System's Defensive Wisdom
concepts.excerpt: Cross-Domain Mechanism: Psychology explains why defensive patterns exist (the meaning, the original threat, what the person is protecting against).
